svg.title: The three service protection API limits and what a throttled client does
svg.desc: Three boxes, each counted per user and per web server. Number of requests: 6,000 in the preceding 300 seconds; error 0x80072322; typical cause one request per row; remedy fewer reads and batching. Execution time: 1,200 seconds of combined server time in the preceding 300 seconds; error 0x80072321; typical cause large batches, heavy synchronous plug-ins or long requests in parallel; remedy smaller batches and less parallelism. Concurrent requests: 52 or more at the same moment; error 0x80072326; typical cause unbounded parallel loops; remedy cap parallelism at the recommended degree. Below, a timeline: a client sends requests; the sliding window always covers the last five minutes; one request is answered 429 with Retry-After 37; the client sends nothing for 37 seconds and then repeats that request and continues. A final note: the licence entitlement is a separate allowance that counts data changes over 24 hours.
svg.text: Per user, per web server: three limits that close each other's loopholes
one request per row, per-row lookups
1,200 s of server time in 300 seconds
What the client sees and does
sliding window: always the preceding 5 minutes, per web server
Not the same thing: the licence entitlement (Power Platform requests) counts data changes over 24 hours. Batching does not reduce it.
